headline: State desk: Houston deprioritises marijuana; NJ workers unionise
dek: Houston adds voter-approved marijuana deprioritisation to its charter, TerrAscend workers in New Jersey join UFCW, and Illinois and Texas widen pickup options.
key_points: Houston City Council amended the city charter on 17 November to make misdemeanor marijuana possession the police's lowest priority, after 423,244 voters backed Proposition A.
Houston police arrested about 440 people a year for misdemeanor possession under Mayor John Whitmire, versus an average of about 35 a year in 2021 to 2023, Houston Public Media found.
Workers at TerrAscend's Apothecarium dispensary in Phillipsburg, New Jersey, voted to join UFCW Local 360.
Terrabis opened its third Illinois drive-through, and Texas Original won approval for a satellite medical dispensary in Fort Worth.
body: Houston has written marijuana deprioritisation into its city charter. The City Council amended the charter on 17 November to make enforcement of Class A and Class B misdemeanor marijuana possession the Houston Police Department's lowest priority and to ban no-knock warrants permanently, two weeks after voters approved Proposition A, Houston Public Media reported.

Elsewhere on the state desk, workers at a TerrAscend dispensary in New Jersey voted to unionise, an Illinois operator opened its third drive-through window, and a Texas medical provider gained a satellite store under the state's expanded programme.

Proposition A passed with more than 70% of the vote, 423,244 to 168,961, according to Houston Public Media. The measure reached the ballot after the progressive group Ground Game Texas gathered more than 40,000 petition signatures. It also enshrines a no-knock warrant ban that HPD adopted as policy in 2019 after the deadly Harding Street raid.

The numbers behind the vote are stark. Under Mayor John Whitmire, who took office in 2024, Houston police have arrested about 440 people a year for misdemeanor marijuana possession, up from an average of about 35 a year from 2021 to 2023, according to data Houston Public Media obtained. By our arithmetic, that is more than twelve times the earlier rate. The Harris County District Attorney's Office also raised misdemeanor marijuana prosecutions to more than 1,600 in 2024, from an average of 151 in the three years before.

The charter change does not legalise anything. Under Texas law, possessing four ounces or less remains a misdemeanor that can lead to arrest, and HPD had not said how the amendment would change its policy, the station reported. Before Election Day, Whitmire and Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare both said misdemeanor marijuana was not a local enforcement priority, according to Houston Public Media; the arrest and prosecution figures are what voters weighed against those statements. The vote adds pressure on the state legislature, where, as we have reported, Democrats are preparing legalisation bills for 2027.
> Houston voters can tell their police what to ignore, but only Austin can change what is legal.

Workers at The Apothecarium in Phillipsburg, a dispensary owned by TerrAscend, voted to join United Food and Commercial Workers Local 360, the union said in a 17 November release. The vote starts negotiations toward a first contract covering wages, benefits and conditions. UFCW, which describes itself as the cannabis union recognised by the AFL-CIO, has made multistate operators a focus of its organising. Local 360 president Sam Ferraino said any company with a national footprint should commit to good local jobs.

The vote follows, as we reported on 17 November, a strike authorisation by workers at Sweet Flower in Los Angeles ahead of Green Wednesday. Organised labour is becoming a bigger factor in operators' costs just as federal tax relief begins to reach registered medical businesses. That is our assessment.

Terrabis said on 18 November that it had opened a drive-through dispensary in Mundelein, in Lake County, its third in Illinois since Senate Bill 3222 allowed dispensaries to offer drive-through and curbside pickup, the company said. Customers order online and collect at the window, which opens at 6 a.m., two hours before the store, and runs to 10 p.m. Terrabis said it plans drive-through service at all five of its Illinois stores as approvals allow; its Illinois windows include the state's first dual-window drive-through, in Grayville, and the first in McHenry County, in Woodstock. It already runs a 24-hour window in O'Fallon, Missouri. As we reported on 17 November, Massachusetts regulators have also voted to move ahead with drive-through sales.
## Texas: a satellite store in Fort Worth

Texas Original said its Fort Worth location at 2812 Horne Street has been approved as a satellite dispensary, giving patients in the Texas Compassionate Use Program (TCUP) in Tarrant County same-day pickup. The company said the change follows House Bill 46, which took effect on 1 September 2025, widened TCUP eligibility, allowed vaporised products and opened the way for satellite locations. The Fort Worth site is open Tuesday to Saturday.

Watch for HPD's written policy under the Houston charter amendment, the first contract talks at the Phillipsburg store, more Illinois and Massachusetts drive-through approvals, and further TCUP satellite approvals as Texas lawmakers prepare for the 2027 session.
